page: Microsoft Azure E128-32ds_v6 is an Edsv6-family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture, 16 physical cores, and 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. This server is equipped with 1024.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 32.0 GB per core. It also includes 7559 GB of local storage and is premium storage capable, though it does not feature any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in memory bandwidth and specific processing tasks. The server achieves a strong rating in memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks, with read speeds of 238.84 GB/sec and write speeds of 137.13 GB/sec. Geekbench testing shows strong single-core and multi-core scores, alongside strong performance in image processing, text processing, and Passmark CPU physics tests. Static web serving throughput is also strong at 44.43 GB/sec. Conversely, stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance, Passmark database operations, and Redis SET operations fall within the average range.

For language model workloads, the server demonstrates strong prompt processing speeds, reaching 2558.78 tokens/sec for a small 135M model and 179.21 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model. However, text generation for the medium 7B model is average at 19.63 tokens/sec, and no data is available for large 70B models. Given the massive 1024.0 GB memory capacity and 7559 GB of local storage, this server is configured for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale databases, and data-dense processing tasks that require high memory-to-CPU ratios without requiring GPU acceleration.
